Pawley, Andrew and Harald Hammarström. 2018. The Trans New Guinea family. In Bill Palmer (ed.), The languages and linguistics of the New Guinea area: a comprehensive guide (The World of Linguistics 4), 21-195. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton. (Open-access chapter, OAPEN handle 20.500.12657/23719, archive.org item oapen-20.500.12657-23719.)
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: For Isabi: documentation inventory only ('wordlist: Z'graggen 1980d') and the reclassification note 'Isabi, previously considered a Madang language, is reclassified as Gorokan by Pawley (2005: 93) and Ross (1995: 146)'. The chapter's tone/pitch accent section (Donohue 1997, Ross 2005b typology; 'In languages of the Madang and Finisterre-Huon groups.. tone and pitch accent are largely absent') names no Isabi data. Confirms independently that no phonological description of Isabi exists as of 2018.

sources.citation: Pawley, Andrew. 2005. The chequered career of the Trans New Guinea hypothesis. In Pawley et al. (eds), Papuan Pasts, 67-107. Pacific Linguistics 572. (p. 93 on Isabi)
sources.note: Glottolog's subclassification source for placing Isabi in Goroka; classification only, unlikely to mention stress, listed for completeness.

sources.citation: Pawley, Andrew. 2001. The Proto Trans New Guinea obstruents: arguments from top-down reconstruction. In Andrew Pawley, Malcolm Ross and Darrell Tryon (eds), The boy from Bundaberg: studies in Melanesian linguistics in honour of Tom Dutton, 261-300. Pacific Linguistics 514. Canberra: Australian National University. (ANU Open Research hdl 1885/254062)
sources.note: Nothing on Isabi prosody. Isabi occurs three times, only as cognate forms in pTNG sets (*tumba(C) 'short' > Isabi simba; *tu 'axe' > Isabi tu; *ka(nd,t)(e,i)[C] 'ear' > Isabi gari). The paper's phonological-typology section states 'A number of TNG languages are tonal, with considerable typological variety in the systems (Donohue 1997), but only segmental phonemes will be considered here', and Isabi is not among the languages whose segment inventories are tabulated. Read from the repository's TEXT bitstream (105 KB) rather than the 3.4 MB PDF.
sources.venue: The boy from Bundaberg: studies in Melanesian linguistics in honour of Tom Dutton

sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. 1980. A comparative word list of the Southern Adelbert Range languages, Madang Province, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics D-33. Canberra: ANU. (Isabi = language I1)
sources.note: Nothing on stress (no occurrence of 'stress'/'accent' in the volume; I1 forms carry no stress or tone marks, visual check printed p. 8). Intro sec. 3, p. vi: 'Isabi and Biyom languages are tonal and they are the only tonal languages so far known within the Adelbert Range language group.' Sec. 9 p. viii-ix: semi-phonemic transcription, Isabi segment fluctuations only.

sources.citation: Wurm, S. A. 1975. The application of the comparative method to Papuan languages: general and Highlands. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 1: Papuan languages and the New Guinea linguistic scene, 237-261. Pacific Linguistics C-38. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Nothing. Isabi is cited only as two cognate forms in pTNG sets: 'Brahman Stock: Isabi gari, Biyom kwa..' (ear, p. 253) and 'Brahman Stock: Isabi ne, Biyom n(a), Tauya ni' (eat, p. 256). No typological or prosodic remark on Isabi in the chapter.
